design.question: Can a complete source argument use kind-qualified animal capacity to reinforce a human directive while keeping the example's actors, the addressee and descriptive/deontic force distinct?

exact_locus.core: verses13–26; example15–23 and downstream cloak directive25–26

source_anchors: 13–14 already direct the reader to govern himself as the time requires.
15–16: Also thünd doch die thier ... die gar kein vernunfft hand.
21–23: wolf/leopard; each according to its kind can preserve itself according to time.
25–26: Deinen mantel soltu keren dar / do yeder winde wähet har.
design.input: Changing conditions and kind-qualified animal self-preservation/capacity, inside an already introduced human conduct instruction.
carried_dependencies: Animal retains its own kind and self-preservation relation; no common action is supplied for all species.
Also connects the animal example to the preceding rule; Deinen/soltu returns to the human addressee and his garment.
The source order is human directive, animal example, renewed/concrete human directive, not observation followed by an actual intervention episode.
design.written_output: A directive addressed to the human reader about turning his cloak in relation to the wind; no claim that the reader complied or was preserved.
proposed_construction: Keep CAN/description and SHOULD/directive separate from ACTUALLY_DID or ACTUALLY_SUCCEEDED.
design.distinguishing_consequence: Animal capacity and the human directive can both be retained without asserting human compliance or success. A rendering that makes animals own the reader's cloak, makes the animals medicinal ingredients, or treats one species' unstated movement as the identical human action changes the source. Flat creature/garment labels omit the written return from example to instruction.
rivals: Merely adjacent animal catalogue and unrelated command.
Animal descriptive facts by themselves logically entail a human obligation.
A fixed compass-bearing transformation derived from the cloak phrase.
interpretive_costs: Reason-giving exemplum is supported discourse interpretation, not an explicitly formal a-fortiori proof rule.
The final word of verse24 and some bird/weather wording remain uncertain; the proposal does not depend on resolving them.
The cloak line's practical/proverbial register is not forced into a target geometry or a universal physical maneuver.
Any target use would need independently justified argument/entity/modality binding; none is supplied here.
